newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom sees cable TV growing 8 pct by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Telekom sees cable TV growing 8 pct by 1998.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG said on Tuesday it expected to expand its cable television network by about eight percent to reach about 18 million homes by 1998 -- a sign growth is slowing.

The network, one of the world's largest, grew 5.5 percent to 16.7 million homes in 1996, the German telephone company said. In the last two years, Telekom added 2.03 million homes to its cable systems, growing 14 percent in that time.

Telekom also said the number of homes with Telekom's cable available to them was expected to rise three percent to about 25.7 million over the next two years. Homes with cable available rose three percent to 24.9 million in 1996.
Of homes with cable available, 66.9 percent are connected, Telekom said.
Telekom has vowed to keep the cable system against critics' complaints that its dual holdings in phone lines and cable TV monopolise access to private homes.

Cable TV lines have been thought a potential alternative to telephone lines for future video conferencing, Internet and other communications services. Some critics in government and industry have called for Telekom to divest its cable business to promote competition.
